title: Coleman Industrial Home: Mr. Moore and the drums
summary: Put in a boarding home with his brother after his father left, he is drawn back to music by teacher Mr. Moore, tries brass horns, and settles on snare drum and marching band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, listen. Tell me why. Did you have brothers and sisters?
Yes, an older brother. He was two years
Because there wasn't anyone to take care of you.
No. My father left. I don't know. And there we were, two boys......

With no mother. So an uncle put us away in a place called the Coleman Industrial Home, where there were some excellent musicians. I was really -- I couldn't believe it. And the teacher, Mr. Moore, he was capable of playing all the instruments. And then I became interested in music again because I loved him so much.
Well, how wonderful. What age did you become interested again?
As early as that. We -- well, they had a marching band there.
And Mr. Moore knew of my musical background. He knew that I could solfegge. He knew that I could read a little bit. So then he started me to playing the alto horn, the peck horn as we called it.
Yeah. And from there I went to the baritone horn and then the trumpet, and the trombone, until, well, the brass instruments just didn't appeal to me like I thought they would.

And he says, 'Well, Kenny, why don't you try the drums, why don't you try to play marches.' So he taught me the drums. You know, the snare drums. And I began to play, to march and play with the band. And then I guess -- I imagine I was about 11, and then there was a completely hiatus. I just -- I don't know what happened. I just seemed to have forgot about music entirely until I was about 17. Just completely faded away after I left there. My stepfather took me away from there.
